To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the density of states of a p-brane grows exponentially in a formal limit, p → ∞, which is the limit of a black hole.

1) The asymptotic density of states for the p-branes is computed and found to grow exponentially in p, 2) the entropy is computed and found not to scale like S ∼ A p, 3) the thermodynamic stability of the p-branes in the large p limit is discussed, and 4) the thermodynamics of the p-brane is discussed in the context of the thermodynamics of black holes.
we have computed the asymptotic density of states of p-branes in the semi-classical limit, and that we have obtained a value that only resembles the exponential of black holes in this formal limit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the density of quantum states of p-branes in string theory.
the study of p-branes, objects which have attracted a lot of attention in recent years due to their relevance in string theory.
the study of p-brane thermodynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the density of states of p-branes grows as exp (p ^{2/3} ) for large values of p.
the p-brane is an asymptotically flat, non-extremal object with an entropy that increases with p.

the p-branes do not exhibit a thermodynamical behaviour which is similar to that of the black holes, and that the thermodynamics of the p-branes is not a good model to study black hole thermodynamics, as it is usually done.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the asymptotic density of states of a p-brane in the semi-classical limit p → ∂ is the same as the one for a black hole of the same dimension.
the density of states of p-brane systems are very much like the one of black holes in a formal sense, but not in a physical one.
the p-brane thermodynamics is not so different from that of black holes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the density of states of p-branes is not exponential.
p-brane thermodynamics does not seem to follow the standard thermodynamic laws, and that this may be a consequence of the fact that p-brane physics is not a classical theory.
the density of states of p-brane is not exponentially increasing, but it grows polynomially in the number of dimensions.
